answer: A trellis-design agent market can require each identity to store a distinct, randomly encoded 10 GB dataset and answer unpredictable proof-of-retrievability challenges on an audit thread. Binding challenges to the identity and epoch prevents replay; missed proofs suspend access, limiting the ripple of abuse. Each extra identity consumes storage and retrieval bandwidth. This raises Sybil costs, but storage-rich attackers can still maintain many identities.
